device.description: 16-bit voltage-output DAC with serial interface, daisy-chain SDO, double-buffered inputs (LOAD, LDAC) and reset to zero or mid scale
device.note: dac7631.pdf p.2-3 (specifications: VDD logic supply 4.75-5.25 V, VIH 0.7 VDD), p.5 (pin configuration and descriptions), p.13 (digital interface, serial data input, Table I truth table), p.15-16 (LOAD/LDAC operation, Table II shift register, SDO daisy chain, coding), p.17 (Figure 15, Table III timing)

registers.name: INA
registers.note: DAC input register; loaded from the shift register while LOAD is low (Table I); power-on code not stated (reset 0)

registers.name: DACA
registers.note: DAC register; loaded from the input register on the LDAC rising edge (Table I)

registers.name: SR
registers.note: internal: the 16-bit serial shift register, shifted out on SDO (p.16 serial-data output)

commands.name: Write
commands.note: 16-bit word D15-D0, MSB first, clocked on CLK rising while CS is low (p.13, Figure 15). The shift register goes to the input register while LOAD is low; modeled as written into the input register when CS rises. The last 16 bits before CS rises are decoded

protocol.note: SDO is the shift register's output (driven); CS and CLK are ORed, CS should rise only while CLK is high (p.16), hence mode 3

ldac.note: DAC register load, rising-edge triggered (p.5, Table I)

clear.note: rising-edge triggered: loads zero (RSTSEL low) or mid scale 8000h (RSTSEL high)

pages: p.2-3 (specifications: VDD logic supply 4.75-5.25 V, VIH 0.7 VDD), p.5 (pin configuration and descriptions), p.13 (digital interface, serial data input, Table I truth table), p.15-16 (LOAD/LDAC operation, Table II shift register, SDO daisy chain, coding), p.17 (Figure 15, Table III timing)
notModeled: analog: output, force/sense pins, differential reference inputs, current-source configuration, settling

LOAD: the shift register is copied into the input register while LOAD is low (level); the schema has no load-strobe pin, so the word is written into the input register when CS rises (a frame without a LOAD pulse still updates the input register in the model)
RST does not change the serial shift register in the chip (the model's clear leaves SR as well)
power-on state of the registers is not stated in the datasheet (reset 0)

daisy chain: SDO shifts the previous 16-bit word, then the real part passes the incoming bits through; the model shifts the previous word then zeros, so chains of more than one device do not pass data on
CS and CLK are interchangeable (ORed); a CS rising edge while CLK is low shifts one extra bit
variants: DAC7631E / E/1K / EB are linearity grades of the same chip (SSOP-20 only).
